children: The National Bank of Poland kept its main interest rate at 3.75% on Wednesday, maintaining its cautious approach as rising commodity prices and increased energy costs create a risk of higher inflation.

The decision by the Monetary Policy Council (MPC) is in line with economists' expectations. All 29 respondents in a Reuters poll forecast that the NBP would keep its main interest rate (PLNINT=ECI) at 3.75% in September.
Inflation rose to 3.4% on the year in August, more than expected by analysts and nearing the top end of the central bank's target range of 1.5% to 3.5%.
"The Monetary Policy Council kept interest rates unchanged, while the balance of risks to inflation has shifted upwards," wrote Rafal Benecki, Chief Economist at ING in Poland, in a commentary.
"Rising oil prices, geopolitical tensions, and the risk of higher energy costs in 2027 argue for a cautious approach by the central bank."
He added that inflation could approach 4% in the coming months and expected interest rates to remain unchanged in the coming quarters.
Analysts also point out that loose fiscal policy is a factor that potentially limits any easing of monetary policy.
A draft budget for 2027 projected that the general government deficit-to-GDP ratio will remain unchanged next year at 7.1% and will ease only marginally from 7.3% in 2025.

The market is now waiting for the statement after the MPC meeting, which will be published on Wednesday afternoon, as well as for Thursday's press conference with the NBP governor, who will justify the central bank's decisions.

Governor Adam Glapinski said in July he could propose a 25-basis-point interest rate cut after the summer, adding though that other Monetary Policy Council members could prove more cautious about further monetary easing.
The bank last cut interest rates in March.
